_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 2 Science unit lecture film, Lesson 8 Electricity and Circuits. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON['lecture'] in content/lesson-8.py part by part, in its own words, and the lesson's steps in their order: its electric helpers (a lamp, a kettle, cooking, a fridge, a toy car, a radio); its safety rules and the Safe / Not safe sort; its circuit, built part by part as its build step builds it (ART.kit.circuitSvg: the cell, a wire, the lamp, the second wire), then broken with a gap and mended; the torch, its picture and its diagram, with the lesson's own symbols; and the torch's switch, a gap you open and close (its 'How a torch works' step, 2SIC.02).
title: Electricity and Circuits
subtitle: Grade 2 Science
objectives: Identify how we use electricity and describe how to be safe with it.
Recognise the components of simple circuits (limited to cells, wires and lamps).
Explore the construction of simple series circuits (limited to cells, wires and lamps).
Follow instructions safely when doing practical work.
Know that a model represents an object or idea in a clear way.
Make and use a physical model of a familiar system or idea.
Describe the difference between a diagram and a picture.
Talk about how science explains how objects they use, or know about, work.

beats.say: Electricity lights a lamp. It has to flow all the way round a loop.
That loop is a circuit. You can build one, and make a lamp light.
Electricity does jobs for us all day. A lamp turns it into light.
A kettle turns it into heat. A cooker cooks our food.
A fridge uses it to keep food cold. A toy car uses it to move.
A radio turns it into sound. Electricity is not only for lights.
The electricity in a wall socket is strong. It can hurt you badly.
Only a plug goes in a socket. Never poke one with a pencil.
Dry hands on switches. Water lets electricity through to you.
Never fly a kite near power lines. If a wire is broken, tell a grown-up.
A small cell is safe to hold. Never put it in your mouth.
Follow the rules when you build a circuit, and you are safe.
A simple circuit has three parts: a cell, wires and a lamp.
The cell is a small battery. It pushes the electricity round.
Add a wire, then the lamp. The lamp is not lit yet.
Add the second wire to close the loop. Now the lamp lights!
That loop is a circuit. Electricity flows out of the cell, through the lamp, and back.
Your circuit is a model of a torch. Now take one wire out.
The lamp goes out. There is a gap, so the loop is broken.
Electricity can only flow round a complete loop. A gap anywhere, and it stops.
Put the wire back. The loop is complete, and the lamp lights again.
Look inside a real torch: a battery, two metal strips and a little lamp.
A picture shows how the torch looks. It does not show the loop inside.
A diagram uses symbols. A long line and a short line stand for the cell.
A circle with a cross is the lamp. Straight lines are the wires.
The diagram is a model of the torch. It shows the loop clearly.
A torch has a switch. A switch is a gap you can open and close.
Switch it on, and the loop closes. The lamp lights.
Switch it off, and a gap opens. The lamp goes out.
Electricity does jobs for us all day. Rules keep you safe with it.
A cell, wires and a lamp in a complete loop make a circuit. A gap stops it.

at.parts: A cell, wires and a lamp

beats.say: A switch opens and closes a gap. A diagram is a model of the circuit.
